Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions are to register for the queue in advance by pressing *1-1. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; and Taylor Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results may differ materially due to a variety of factors. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI CodeGen module and continued execution of our strategic initiatives across our AI-powered DevOps platform, which delivers next-generation CI/CD pipelines with integrated MLOps to help enterprises accelerate from code commit to production.

Our focus this quarter was on four key areas: accelerating ARR growth, sustaining elite NRR performance, optimizing our operating expense structure for leverage, and setting a strong foundation for next quarter's momentum.

On ARR growth, we delivered another standout quarter that outpaced our peers and highlighted the power of our land-and-expand model. NRR remained a key strength, reflecting deep customer stickiness amid AI transformation waves. We maintained tight discipline on operating expenses to fuel innovation without sacrificing margins. And looking ahead, our guidance positions us for continued acceleration.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $112 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin expanded to 79%, and non-GAAP operating income reached $18 million, reflecting healthy profitability as we scale.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 FY2024 earnings call. As we dive into our financial results, I'd like to start with our core growth engine: Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR. ARR remains the north star metric for SaaS businesses like ours here at CloudForge, where we deliver our market-leading AI-powered DevOps platform—think next-gen CI/CD pipelines with integrated ML ops, helping enterprises like Fortune 500 tech firms accelerate from code commit to production at unprecedented speeds.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2024, we ended with total ARR of $452 million, up an impressive 29% year-over-year from $350 million in Q3 FY2023, and 7% quarter-over-quarter from $422 million at the end of Q2 FY2024. This marks our 11th straight quarter of at least 25% YoY ARR growth, outpacing the public SaaS cohort average of around 18% as reported by Bessemer Venture Partners' latest Cloud Index.

Let me unpack this for you with some color on the drivers, breakdowns, and what it means strategically. First, on the YoY dynamics: This 29% growth reflects a powerful mix of new logo acquisition and expansion within our land-and-expand model. We added $28 million in net new ARR from approximately 150 new customers, with an average ACV of $187,000—our highest in two years, driven by larger enterprise deals. Think multi-year contracts with embedded commitments for our new ForgeAI CodeGen module, which automates 40% of boilerplate code generation using generative AI, similar to how GitHub Copilot has transformed developer productivity but tailored for enterprise-scale pipelines.

Expansions contributed another $74 million, fueled by a 124% net retention rate for the quarter—up from 118% a year ago. Our dollar-based net expansion rate hit 132%, as customers upsell into advanced features like our autonomous testing suite and Kubernetes-native deployment orchestration. Churn remained elite at under 4% gross dollar churn, well below the industry benchmark of 7-8% for enterprise SaaS, thanks to our focus on customer success playbooks and proactive health scoring.

QoQ growth of 7% was slightly ahead of our internal guide of 6-7%, accelerating from 6% in Q2. This sequential uptick signals improving macro tailwinds: despite ongoing enterprise budget scrutiny reminiscent of the 2022 reset, we're seeing green shoots in non-tech verticals. Net new ARR was $30 million, with expansions adding $22 million—highlighting the stickiness of our platform as customers deepen usage amid AI-fueled digital transformation waves.

Regional commentary: North America remains our powerhouse, contributing 68% of total ARR at $308 million, up 32% YoY on massive wins with hyperscalers and Big Tech—echoing the AWS-Outposts style integrations we've rolled out. EMEA grew 45% YoY to $82 million (18% of total), propelled by GDPR-compliant AI features and key logos in financial services, like a Tier-1 European bank standardizing on our platform post their legacy Jenkins migration. APAC is our fastest grower at 52% YoY to $62 million (14% of total), with strong traction in Japan and India; we just announced a strategic partnership with NTT Data to bundle our tools into their sovereign cloud offerings, targeting the $10B+ APAC DevOps TAM.

Strategically, these results underscore three key initiatives propelling us forward: AI Monetization, where our ForgeAI suite, launched at our inaugural CloudForge Summit in June, drove 40% of new ARR. Early adopters are seeing 3x faster release cycles, akin to Datadog's AI guardrails but for the full SDLC. We've already priced premium tiers at a 25% uplift, with 85% adoption among Q3 new logos. Enterprise Motion Refinement: We've doubled down on 'bowling pin' sales—starting with mid-market CI/CD wins and expanding to full-stack observability. This yielded 15 deals over $1M ACV, including a landmark $5M expansion with a leading semiconductor firm automating their edge AI deployments. And Market Tailwinds: Broader industry trends like the shift to agentic AI workflows (per Gartner’s 2024 Magic Quadrant positioning us as a Visionary) and regulatory pushes for secure supply chains are creating urgency. We're also benefiting from M&A consolidation; post our acquisition of PipelinePro last year, we've cross-sold into 60% of their base.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 ARR to land between $475-485 million, implying 26-28% YoY growth and 5-7% QoQ. This guidance bakes in some forex headwinds in EMEA but is underpinned by a $2.1 billion RPO—up 35% YoY—with 92% current RPO coverage. We're well-positioned to sustain 25%+ growth into FY2025 as we execute on these initiatives.

Thank you, Alex. Now, turning to our outlook for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024, ending December 31st. We are guiding to quarter-end ARR of $475 million to $485 million, representing sequential growth of 5% to 7% from the $452 million we reported at the end of Q3. On a year-over-year basis, this implies approximately 26% to 28% growth, accelerating from the 29% YoY we delivered in Q3.

Let me break this down by the key drivers, as we continue to execute on our land-and-expand playbook in a market that's showing signs of stabilization after the tech spending pullback we saw in late 2023 and early 2024. First, new logo acquisition remains our growth engine. We're expecting $20 million to $22 million in new ARR from net new customers, fueled by our recent launches in the AI-native DevOps space. Specifically, our CloudForge Agentic Orchestrator—our generative AI platform for autonomous CI/CD pipelines, which integrates seamlessly with models like Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's GPT-4o—has seen explosive adoption. We've already landed pilots with three Fortune 500 enterprises in Q3, including a major fintech player akin to Stripe, and we're forecasting conversion rates north of 70% in Q4 as these go live.

Expansion within our existing base is equally robust, with projected upsell and cross-sell ARR of $14 million to $16 million. Our Net Revenue Retention held steady at 124% in Q3, and we're guiding for 123% to 125% this quarter. This is driven by our strategic focus on multi-product adoption: customers using our core GitFlow platform alongside our new Sentinel Security module—our zero-trust compliance tool certified for SOC 2 Type II and FedRAMP Moderate—are expanding 2.5x faster than single-product users. We've seen particular strength in healthcare and financial services verticals, where regulatory tailwinds like the EU's DORA framework are pushing upgrades.

On churn and contraction, we're maintaining our dollar-based churn below 4% annually, with expansion cohorts more than offsetting any macroeconomic noise. While we've noted some budget scrutiny in SMB segments, we're countering this with our FlexScale pricing model, which allows usage-based scaling similar to Snowflake's consumption pricing, keeping expansion velocity high.

Regionally, the Americas will contribute about 65% of our Q4 bookings growth, anchored by hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure. We've expanded our AWS Marketplace presence, driving a 40% YoY increase in co-sell deals. EMEA is our fastest-growing theater at 40% YoY ARR growth guidance, benefiting from GDPR-aligned features in Sentinel and wins in the DACH region, including a landmark deal with a Siemens-scale industrial manufacturer. APAC rounds out at 30% YoY, tempered by FX headwinds from a stronger USD, but offset by our Tokyo data center launch and traction with Japanese telcos mirroring NTT's cloud migration playbook.

From a technical standpoint, our Q4 guidance embeds investments in edge computing integrations and Kubernetes-native observability, positioning us ahead of competitors like Harness or GitLab in the agentic AI DevOps wave. We've allocated $18 million of our opex to R&D here, expecting ROI through a 15-20% uplift in deal velocity from proof-of-concepts converting to multi-year contracts.

Strategically, we're prioritizing large enterprise deals—those over $1 million ACV—which represented 50% of Q3 bookings and are projected at 55% in Q4. This mirrors the playbook of high-flyers like Datadog and CrowdStrike, where depth in the Fortune 1000 drives durable growth. Macro conditions remain constructive: Gartner forecasts SaaS spending growth accelerating to 12% in 2025 from 8% this year, and our Rule of 40 score of 55% in Q3 gives us ample runway to navigate any lingering caution.

We're confident in this guide, with a bias to the upside as our pipeline sits at $2.1 billion—up 20% quarter-over-quarter—and sales productivity metrics like quota attainment at 105%.

Thank you, Alex. Now, turning to our operating expense breakdown for Q3 FY2024, I'm pleased to report that we continue to demonstrate strong expense discipline amid robust revenue growth of 28% year-over-year to $112 million. Total non-GAAP operating expenses came in at $94 million, up just 15% year-over-year, which reflects our focus on operational leverage as we scale. As a percentage of revenue, op-ex declined to 84% from 89% a year ago, driving meaningful expansion in our adjusted operating margin to 20%—well on track toward our long-term target of 30%+ as we approach Rule of 40 territory with a score of 48 this quarter.

Let me drill down into the key line items: R&D, Sales & Marketing, and G&A. Starting with R&D, which was $34 million, or 30% of revenue, up 20% year-over-year. This increase was purposeful and ties directly to our strategic investments in next-generation AI capabilities within our CloudForge Analytics platform. Specifically, we've accelerated development on our GenAI Copilot—think Salesforce Einstein meets Microsoft Copilot, but purpose-built for enterprise data orchestration—which is now in beta with 15 early customers, including two Fortune 100 names in financial services. Headcount in R&D grew modestly by 12% quarter-over-quarter to 450 engineers, with about 40% of that team now dedicated to machine learning ops (MLOps) and large language model (LLM) fine-tuning on hyperscaler infrastructure like AWS Bedrock and Azure OpenAI.

Regionally, we're seeing R&D efficiencies from our new Dublin engineering hub, which handles 25% of our EMEA-focused localization efforts, reducing latency for our EU customers under GDPR compliance. That said, we expect R&D to moderate to 28-29% of revenue in the back half as these initiatives mature and we leverage open-source frameworks like LangChain and Hugging Face to optimize costs. This positions us competitively against the likes of Databricks and Snowflake, who are also pouring billions into AI lakehouses, but our edge is in seamless SaaS integration without rip-and-replace migrations.

Moving to Sales & Marketing, at $42 million, or 38% of revenue, up 10% year-over-year—our slowest growth rate in S&M in five quarters. This reflects the power of our product-led growth (PLG) motion, where we've shifted 35% of new ARR from self-serve trials via our freemium tier, driving customer acquisition costs (CAC) down 18% to $4,200 per net new ARR dollar. Sales efficiency remains stellar at 1.2x, with payback periods compressing to 14 months from 18 months last year.

Breaking it out, marketing spend was $14 million (down 5% YoY), fueled by high-ROI channels like intent-based advertising on platforms akin to 6sense and Demandbase, which captured mid-market leads in verticals like healthcare and manufacturing. Sales was $28 million (up 14% YoY), with expansions driving 65% of total bookings—classic land-and-expand in enterprise accounts. Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse at 70% of S&M allocation, but we're ramping EMEA to 20% with a new London sales pod targeting DACH compliance-heavy deals, and APAC at 10% via partnerships with Alibaba Cloud for joint go-to-market in Southeast Asia. Compared to peers like HubSpot or Zendesk, our S&M as a percentage of revenue is trending below the SaaS median of 42%, and we guide for further leverage to 35% by FY2025 through AI-powered sales assist tools that automate 30% of pipeline qualification.

Finally, G&A at $18 million, or 16% of revenue, was essentially flat year-over-year—a testament to our rigorous cost controls. This includes $7 million in people costs for our 200-strong HQ functions, with headcount growth capped at 2% amid a company-wide hiring freeze on non-core roles. Legal and compliance ticked up slightly to $3 million due to one-time expenses around our SOC 2 Type II recertification and preparations for potential ISO 27001 expansion, critical for our growing public sector pipeline.

Stock-based compensation across op-ex was $10 million, or 9% of revenue, down as a percentage due to favorable grant vesting schedules. Overall, these trends underscore our ability to invest aggressively in growth drivers like AI innovation while delivering scalable unit economics—non-GAAP free cash flow margins hit 25% this quarter, up from 20% last year. We're not just keeping up with macro headwinds like elevated interest rates curbing enterprise budgets; we're outpacing them, much like how ServiceNow navigated post-pandemic spend scrutiny.

Thank you, Alex. Moving to our core SaaS metrics, I'm pleased to report that our dollar-based Net Revenue Retention—or NRR—came in at 124% for Q3, marking a sequential improvement from 118% in Q2 and a robust 12-point expansion year-over-year from 112% in Q3 last year. This performance underscores the strength of our land-and-expand model in a still-challenging macro environment, where enterprise customers continue to consolidate spend on mission-critical platforms like ours. For context, this places us at the high end of our public SaaS peers—think Snowflake's recent 114% or Databricks' mid-110s—driven by sticky usage in our AI-powered data analytics platform.

Let me break this down by the key drivers: expansion, which contributed +32 points; offset by churn at -3 points and contraction at -5 points. Starting from our Q3 opening ARR cohort of $1.4 billion, this translated to $420 million in retained and expanded revenue from existing customers alone—representing over 70% of our total ARR growth this quarter.

Expansion was the standout at 32% net expansion rate, fueled by several strategic levers. First, our new AI Co-Pilot module, launched in late Q2 and inspired by innovations like Salesforce Einstein or Adobe Sensei, saw adoption rates exceed 40% among eligible enterprise customers. This drove upsell ACV increases averaging 25% per account, particularly in cross-sells from our core data warehousing to advanced ML workflows. We saw seat expansion in 62% of our top 500 customers, as teams scaled usage amid generative AI pilots—think replacing point solutions like custom Tableau dashboards with our unified platform. Regionally, North America led with 35% expansion, thanks to hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure, while EMEA grew to 28% on stronger compliance features for GDPR-heavy verticals like financial services. Even in APAC, we hit 25%, up from 20% YoY, as we ramped localization for Japan and Australia.

Churn remained low at 3% logo churn and 3% revenue churn, well below our historical 5-6% average and industry benchmarks from Bessemer’s Cloud Index. This resilience held despite SMB headwinds from higher interest rates—our < $100K ACV segment saw elevated churn at 6%, primarily non-renewals in marketing tech amid ad spend cuts. However, enterprise churn (< $1M ACV) was negligible at 1%, bolstered by our Customer Success 2.0 program, which includes proactive health scoring via our own platform's predictive analytics. We've reduced at-risk accounts by 30% through automated renewal playbooks, similar to how HubSpot refined theirs post-IPO.

Contraction ticked up slightly to 5% from 4% last quarter, largely due to optimization in mid-market accounts—customers right-sizing post-pandemic over-provisioning, akin to what we've seen across the sector with Zoom or Slack usage normalization. Usage-based pricing helped mitigate this, limiting revenue contraction to 3% net, as high-usage cohorts like manufacturing (with our IoT analytics) expanded mid-term. APAC saw the highest contraction at 7%, tied to forex volatility and slower decision cycles in China, but we're countering this with a new Tokyo data center going live in Q4.

Looking ahead, our cohort analysis shows improving vintage curves: the Q1 '24 cohort is tracking at 125% NRR at the 6-month mark, versus 115% for Q1 '23—evidence that our platform investments are compounding. Strategically, we're doubling down on vertical-specific expansions, like healthcare integrations with FHIR standards to capture Epic and Cerner migrations, and pricing tiers optimized for AI workloads to sustain 120%+ NRR through 2025. We expect Q4 NRR in the 122-125% range, with expansion holding above 30% as macroeconomic stabilization supports SMB recovery.

Overall, this NRR trajectory validates our focus on product-led growth in a Cohere- and Anthropic-powered AI era, where customers prioritize platforms that scale intelligence without rip-and-replace.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $350 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first three quarters of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $445 million to $455 million, with ARR ending the year at $475-485 million.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press *1-1. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI CodeGen on your overall growth?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI CodeGen has been a game-changer, automating 40% of boilerplate code generation and driving 40% of our new ARR this quarter. It's embedded in multi-year enterprise contracts, boosting average ACV to $187,000—our highest in years. Customers are seeing 3x faster release cycles, leading to premium tier adoption at 85% among new logos and expansions contributing $74 million in ARR. This positions us perfectly in the agentic AI DevOps wave.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Lisa. International remains a high-conviction priority. EMEA grew 45% YoY to $82 million, driven by GDPR-compliant features and wins like a Tier-1 European bank migrating from Jenkins. APAC surged 52% to $62 million, anchored by our NTT Data partnership targeting sovereign cloud in Japan and India. We're ramping sales pods in London for DACH and expanding AWS Marketplace co-sell, expecting EMEA at 40% YoY and APAC 30% in Q4 guidance. Our Tokyo data center and vertical plays in financial services will accelerate this to 35% of total ARR by FY2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan.

Mike Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Mike. Churn stayed elite at under 4% gross dollar, or 3% revenue churn, well below industry 7-8%. Enterprise is negligible at 1%, thanks to Customer Success 2.0 with predictive health scoring reducing at-risk accounts 30%. SMB saw some pressure at 6% from budget scrutiny, but expansions at 32% more than offset, delivering 124% NRR. FlexScale usage pricing and proactive playbooks keep us resilient, with Q4 guide at 122-125% NRR.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
